chapters.title: From Adam to Israel and Edom
chapters.html:
1 Chronicles 1

From Adam to Noah

1Adam, Seth, Enosh,

2Kenan, Mahalalel, Jared,

3Enoch, Methuselah, Lamech,

4Noah, Shem, Ham and Japheth.

The Sons of Noah

5The sons of Japheth: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech and Tiras.

6The sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, Diphath and Togarmah.

7The sons of Javan: Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim and Rodanim.

8The sons of Ham: Cush, Egypt, Put and Canaan.

9The sons of Cush: Seba, Havilah, Sabta, Raama and Sabteca. The sons of Raama: Sheba and Dedan.

10Cush fathered Nimrod. He began to be a mighty one in the earth.

11Egypt fathered the Ludim, the Anamim, the Lehabim and the Naphtuhim,

12the Pathrusim, the Casluhim, from whom the Philistines came, and the Caphtorim.

13Canaan fathered Sidon his firstborn, and Heth,

14and the Jebusite, the Amorite, the Girgashite,

15the Hivite, the Arkite, the Sinite,

16the Arvadite, the Zemarite and the Hamathite.

17The sons of Shem: Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud, Aram, Uz, Hul, Gether and Meshech.

18Arpachshad fathered Shelah, and Shelah fathered Eber.

19To Eber were born two sons. The name of the one was Peleg, for in his days the earth was divided; and the name of his brother was Joktan.

20Joktan fathered Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth and Jerah,

21Hadoram, Uzal and Diklah,

22Ebal, Abimael and Sheba,

23Ophir, Havilah and Jobab. All these were the sons of Joktan.

From Shem to Abraham

24Shem, Arpachshad, Shelah,

25Eber, Peleg, Reu,

26Serug, Nahor, Terah,

27Abram, that is, Abraham.

The Sons of Abraham

28The sons of Abraham: Isaac and Ishmael.

29These are their generations: the firstborn of Ishmael, Nebaioth; then Kedar, Adbeel and Mibsam,

30Mishma, Dumah, Massa, Hadad and Tema,

31Jetur, Naphish and Kedemah. These are the sons of Ishmael.

32The sons of Keturah, Abraham's secondary wife: she bore Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak and Shuah. The sons of Jokshan: Sheba and Dedan.

33The sons of Midian: Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida and Eldaah. All these were the sons of Keturah.

34Abraham fathered Isaac. The sons of Isaac: Esau and Israel.

Esau and Seir

35The sons of Esau: Eliphaz, Reuel, Jeush, Jalam and Korah.

36The sons of Eliphaz: Teman, Omar, Zephi, Gatam, Kenaz, Timna and Amalek.

37The sons of Reuel: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah and Mizzah.

38The sons of Seir: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer and Dishan.

39The sons of Lotan: Hori and Homam; and Lotan's sister was Timna.

40The sons of Shobal: Alian, Manahath, Ebal, Shephi and Onam. The sons of Zibeon: Aiah and Anah.

41The son of Anah: Dishon. The sons of Dishon: Hamran, Eshban, Ithran and Cheran.

42The sons of Ezer: Bilhan, Zaavan and Jaakan. The sons of Dishon: Uz and Aran.

The Kings and Chiefs of Edom

43These are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom before any king reigned over the sons of Israel: Bela son of Beor, and the name of his city was Dinhabah.

44Bela died, and Jobab son of Zerah of Bozrah reigned in his place.

45Jobab died, and Husham of the land of the Temanites reigned in his place.

46Husham died, and Hadad son of Bedad, who struck Midian in the field of Moab, reigned in his place, and the name of his city was Avith.

47Hadad died, and Samlah of Masrekah reigned in his place.

48Samlah died, and Shaul of Rehoboth-on-the-River reigned in his place.

49Shaul died, and Baal-hanan son of Achbor reigned in his place.

50Baal-hanan died, and Hadad reigned in his place, and the name of his city was Pai, and his wife's name was Mehetabel daughter of Matred daughter of Me-zahab.

51Hadad died. The chiefs of Edom were: chief Timna, chief Alvah, chief Jetheth,

52chief Oholibamah, chief Elah, chief Pinon,

53chief Kenaz, chief Teman, chief Mibzar,

54chief Magdiel, chief Iram. These are the chiefs of Edom.

Notes

  • vv1–4 "Adam, Seth, Enosh" — the book opens with bare names, no verbs: the line of Genesis 5 from Adam to Noah in thirteen words. Cain and Abel are left out; only the line that goes on is named.

  • vv5–23 "The sons of Japheth… All these were the sons of Joktan" — the Table of Nations of Genesis 10, nearly word for word, without its comments on the coastlands, Nimrod's kingdom and the borders of Canaan.

  • vv6, 7, 17, 22 "Diphath… Rodanim… Meshech… Ebal" — where Genesis 10 has Riphath, Dodanim, Mash and Obal. The Hebrew letters d and r are written almost alike; the Greek here has Riphath and Rhodians. The text keeps the Hebrew of Chronicles.

  • v17 "Uz, Hul, Gether and Meshech" — in Genesis these are the sons of Aram (Genesis 10:23); Chronicles lists them with Shem's sons. The Greek here stops after Asshur and has nothing for vv18–23.

  • v27 "Abram, that is, Abraham" — Avram hu Avraham: the change of name of Genesis 17:5, in four words.

  • v32 "Keturah, Abraham's secondary wife" — pilegesh. Genesis calls her a wife (Genesis 25:1).

  • v34 "The sons of Isaac: Esau and Israel" — not Jacob: Chronicles calls him by the name God gave him (Genesis 32:28) everywhere but one psalm it quotes (16:13, 17).

  • v36 "Kenaz, Timna and Amalek" — Genesis makes Timna not a son but the secondary wife of Eliphaz and the mother of Amalek (Genesis 36:12); the Greek here reads and of Timna, Amalek. The text keeps the Hebrew list. Chronicles also has Zephi for Zepho, Homam for Hemam in v39, and in vv40–42 Alian, Shephi, Hamran and Jaakan for Genesis's Alvan, Shepho, Hemdan and Akan, and Dishon for Dishan as father of Uz and Aran (v42).

  • vv43–51 "the kings who reigned in the land of Edom… Hadad died" — Genesis 36:31–39. Chronicles has Hadad and Pai for Genesis's Hadar and Pau, and adds Hadad died. Written Ayot, read Avith (v46); written Aliah, read Alvah (v51).

chapters.title: The Sons of Israel and the Line of Judah
chapters.html:
1 Chronicles 2

The Sons of Israel

1These are the sons of Israel: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun,

2Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad and Asher.

Judah

3The sons of Judah: Er, Onan and Shelah; these three were born to him by Bath-shua the Canaanite. Er, Judah's firstborn, was evil in the eyes of the LORD, and He put him to death.

4Tamar his daughter-in-law bore him Perez and Zerah. Judah had five sons in all.

5The sons of Perez: Hezron and Hamul.

6The sons of Zerah: Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Calcol and Dara, five in all.

7The son of Carmi: Achar, the troubler of Israel, who broke faith in what was devoted to destruction.

8The son of Ethan: Azariah.

From Hezron to David

9The sons of Hezron who were born to him: Jerahmeel, Ram and Chelubai.

10Ram fathered Amminadab, and Amminadab fathered Nahshon, leader of the sons of Judah.

11Nahshon fathered Salma, and Salma fathered Boaz.

12Boaz fathered Obed, and Obed fathered Jesse.

13Jesse fathered Eliab his firstborn, Abinadab the second, Shimea the third,

14Nethanel the fourth, Raddai the fifth,

15Ozem the sixth, David the seventh.

16Their sisters were Zeruiah and Abigail. The sons of Zeruiah: Abishai, Joab and Asahel, three.

17Abigail bore Amasa, and the father of Amasa was Jether the Ishmaelite.

Caleb Son of Hezron

18Caleb son of Hezron fathered children by Azubah his wife, and by Jerioth; these were her sons: Jesher, Shobab and Ardon.

19When Azubah died, Caleb took Ephrath, and she bore him Hur.

20Hur fathered Uri, and Uri fathered Bezalel.

21Afterward Hezron went in to the daughter of Machir the father of Gilead, whom he married when he was sixty years old, and she bore him Segub.

22Segub fathered Jair, who had twenty-three cities in the land of Gilead.

23But Geshur and Aram took from them Havvoth-jair, with Kenath and its villages, sixty cities. All these were the sons of Machir the father of Gilead.

24After Hezron died, Caleb went in to Ephrathah. Abijah, Hezron's wife, bore him Ashhur the father of Tekoa.

Jerahmeel

25The sons of Jerahmeel the firstborn of Hezron: Ram the firstborn, Bunah, Oren, Ozem and Ahijah.

26Jerahmeel had another wife, whose name was Atarah; she was the mother of Onam.

27The sons of Ram the firstborn of Jerahmeel: Maaz, Jamin and Eker.

28The sons of Onam: Shammai and Jada. The sons of Shammai: Nadab and Abishur.

29The name of Abishur's wife was Abihail, and she bore him Ahban and Molid.

30The sons of Nadab: Seled and Appaim; Seled died without sons.

31The son of Appaim: Ishi. The son of Ishi: Sheshan. The son of Sheshan: Ahlai.

32The sons of Jada, Shammai's brother: Jether and Jonathan; Jether died without sons.

33The sons of Jonathan: Peleth and Zaza. These were the sons of Jerahmeel.

34Sheshan had no sons, only daughters. Sheshan had an Egyptian servant whose name was Jarha.

35Sheshan gave his daughter to Jarha his servant as wife, and she bore him Attai.

36Attai fathered Nathan, and Nathan fathered Zabad.

37Zabad fathered Ephlal, and Ephlal fathered Obed.

38Obed fathered Jehu, and Jehu fathered Azariah.

39Azariah fathered Helez, and Helez fathered Eleasah.

40Eleasah fathered Sismai, and Sismai fathered Shallum.

41Shallum fathered Jekamiah, and Jekamiah fathered Elishama.

The Sons of Caleb

42The sons of Caleb the brother of Jerahmeel: Mesha his firstborn, who was the father of Ziph. The sons of Mareshah the father of Hebron:

43The sons of Hebron: Korah, Tappuah, Rekem and Shema.

44Shema fathered Raham the father of Jorkeam, and Rekem fathered Shammai.

45The son of Shammai: Maon, and Maon was the father of Beth-zur.

46Ephah, Caleb's secondary wife, bore Haran, Moza and Gazez; and Haran fathered Gazez.

47The sons of Jahdai: Regem, Jotham, Geshan, Pelet, Ephah and Shaaph.

48Maacah, Caleb's secondary wife, bore Sheber and Tirhanah.

49She also bore Shaaph the father of Madmannah, Sheva the father of Machbenah and the father of Gibea. The daughter of Caleb was Achsah.

50These were the sons of Caleb. The sons of Hur the firstborn of Ephrathah: Shobal the father of Kiriath-jearim,

51Salma the father of Bethlehem, and Hareph the father of Beth-gader.

52Shobal the father of Kiriath-jearim had sons: Haroeh, half of the Manahathites.

53The clans of Kiriath-jearim: the Ithrites, the Puthites, the Shumathites and the Mishraites; from these came the Zorathites and the Eshtaolites.

54The sons of Salma: Bethlehem, the Netophathites, Atroth-beth-joab, and half of the Manahathites, the Zorites.

55The clans of the scribes who lived at Jabez: the Tirathites, the Shimeathites and the Sucathites. These are the Kenites who came from Hammath, the father of the house of Rechab.

Notes

  • vv1–2 "These are the sons of Israel" — the twelve in the order of Genesis 35:23–26, except that Dan comes before Joseph and Benjamin. From here to chapter 9 the book is a genealogy, with Judah first and longest.

  • v3 "Er, Judah's firstborn, was evil in the eyes of the LORD, and He put him to death" — Genesis 38:7 word for word, except that Genesis names the LORD a second time, the LORD put him to death. Bath-shua, daughter of Shua: Genesis calls her the daughter of a Canaanite man whose name was Shua (Genesis 38:2).

  • v6 "Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Calcol and Dara" — the wise men Solomon surpassed, Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman, Calcol and Darda (1 Kings 4:31). Joshua calls Zimri Zabdi (Joshua 7:1).

  • v7 "Achar, the troubler of Israel" — Joshua calls him Achan. Chronicles spells the name Akhar to match the verb: okher Yisra'el, who brought trouble on Israel, as Joshua said to him, Why have you brought trouble on us? (Joshua 7:25), and as the valley was named Achor (Joshua 7:26).

  • vv10–12 "Ram fathered Amminadab… Obed fathered Jesse" — the line that closes Ruth (Ruth 4:19–22). Ruth spells Nahshon's son Salmah and Salmon; Chronicles has Salma.

  • vv13–15 "David the seventh" — Samuel says Jesse had eight sons (1 Samuel 17:12); Chronicles names seven, with David last. Shimea is the Shammah of 1 Samuel 16:9.

  • v17 "Jether the Ishmaelite" — Samuel calls Amasa's father Ithra the Israelite (2 Samuel 17:25); the Greek here agrees with Chronicles, the Ishmaelite.

  • v24 "After Hezron died, Caleb went in to Ephrathah" — the Hebrew reads be-Khalev Efratah, in Caleb-ephrathah, as if a place, which is named nowhere else. The Greek has Caleb went in to Ephratha, as if from ba Khalev, one letter more, and v19 has Caleb taking Ephrath as wife. The text follows the Greek.

  • v50 "These were the sons of Caleb. The sons of Hur the firstborn of Ephrathah" — the Hebrew reads ben Chur, son of Hur, which would make Caleb Hur's son; v19 makes Hur Caleb's son, and 4:4 has Hur the firstborn of Ephrathah. The Greek has the sons of Hur, as if from benei Chur, and begins a new list. The text follows the Greek.

  • v55 "the scribes who lived at Jabez… the Kenites… the house of Rechab" — Jehonadab son of Rechab rode with Jehu (2 Kings 10:15). Written yashvu, they lived, read yoshvei, who lived.

chapters.title: The Sons of David and the Kings of Judah
chapters.html:
1 Chronicles 3

The Sons of David

1These were the sons of David who were born to him in Hebron: the firstborn Amnon, by Ahinoam the Jezreelite; the second Daniel, by Abigail the Carmelite;

2the third Absalom, the son of Maacah daughter of Talmai king of Geshur; the fourth Adonijah, the son of Haggith;

3the fifth Shephatiah, by Abital; the sixth Ithream, by Eglah his wife.

4Six were born to him in Hebron, where he reigned seven years and six months. In Jerusalem he reigned thirty-three years.

5These were born to him in Jerusalem: Shimea, Shobab, Nathan and Solomon, four by Bath-shua daughter of Ammiel;

6then Ibhar, Elishama, Eliphelet,

7Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia,

8Elishama, Eliada and Eliphelet, nine.

9All these were the sons of David, besides the sons of the secondary wives; and Tamar was their sister.

The Kings of Judah

10The son of Solomon was Rehoboam; Abijah his son, Asa his son, Jehoshaphat his son,

11Joram his son, Ahaziah his son, Joash his son,

12Amaziah his son, Azariah his son, Jotham his son,

13Ahaz his son, Hezekiah his son, Manasseh his son,

14Amon his son, Josiah his son.

15The sons of Josiah: the firstborn Johanan, the second Jehoiakim, the third Zedekiah, the fourth Shallum.

16The sons of Jehoiakim: Jeconiah his son, Zedekiah his son.

After the Exile

17The sons of Jeconiah the captive: Shealtiel his son,

18Malchiram, Pedaiah, Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama and Nedabiah.

19The sons of Pedaiah: Zerubbabel and Shimei. The sons of Zerubbabel: Meshullam and Hananiah, and Shelomith was their sister;

20and Hashubah, Ohel, Berechiah, Hasadiah and Jushab-hesed, five.

21The sons of Hananiah: Pelatiah and Jeshaiah, the sons of Rephaiah, the sons of Arnan, the sons of Obadiah, the sons of Shecaniah.

22The son of Shecaniah: Shemaiah. The sons of Shemaiah: Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Neariah and Shaphat, six.

23The sons of Neariah: Elioenai, Hizkiah and Azrikam, three.

24The sons of Elioenai: Hodaviah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Delaiah and Anani, seven.

Notes

  • vv1–4 "born to him in Hebron" — the list of 2 Samuel 3:2–5, where the second son is Chileab, not Daniel. Seven years and six months… thirty-three years, as 2 Samuel 5:5.

  • v5 "Shimea… four by Bath-shua daughter of Ammiel" — Samuel has Shammua (2 Samuel 5:14) and calls his mother Bathsheba daughter of Eliam (2 Samuel 11:3). Ammi-el and Eli-am are the same two words, people and God, in the other order. Solomon is named last of the four.

  • vv6–8 "Ibhar, Elishama, Eliphelet, Nogah… Elishama, Eliada and Eliphelet" — two Elishamas and two Eliphelets. Samuel lists Elishua for the first Elishama and has neither the first Eliphelet nor Nogah (2 Samuel 5:15–16); Chronicles' second list has Elishua, Elpelet and Nogah (14:5–7).

  • v15 "the fourth Shallum" — the king called Jehoahaz in Kings (2 Kings 23:30–31); Jeremiah calls him Shallum son of Josiah… who reigned in place of Josiah his father (Jeremiah 22:11). Johanan the firstborn is named nowhere else.

  • v16 "Jeconiah his son, Zedekiah his son" — Jehoiachin, here Jeconiah as in Matthew 1:11. This Zedekiah is a son of Jehoiakim, not the king of 2 Kings 24:17, who was Josiah's son (v15).

  • v17 "Jeconiah the captive" — assir, the prisoner, as Jehoiachin was held in prison in Babylon (2 Kings 25:27). The Greek takes it as a name, Aseir, a son of Jeconiah.

  • v19 "The sons of Pedaiah: Zerubbabel" — Ezra and Haggai call Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel (Ezra 3:2; Haggai 1:1), and so does Matthew (Matthew 1:12); the Greek here reads the sons of Shealtiel: Zerubbabel. The Hebrew of Chronicles makes him Shealtiel's nephew. The text keeps the Hebrew.

  • v22 "Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Neariah and Shaphat, six" — five names and the count six; the Greek also has five names and six. The text keeps both.

  • v24 "Hodaviah" — written Hodayvahu, read Hodavyahu, a spelling difference. The line of David runs on past the return from exile, through Zerubbabel's descendants.

chapters.title: The Clans of Judah and Simeon
chapters.html:
1 Chronicles 4

Judah

1The sons of Judah: Perez, Hezron, Carmi, Hur and Shobal.

2Reaiah son of Shobal fathered Jahath, and Jahath fathered Ahumai and Lahad. These were the clans of the Zorathites.

3These were the sons of Etam: Jezreel, Ishma and Idbash, and the name of their sister was Hazzelelponi;

4and Penuel was the father of Gedor, and Ezer the father of Hushah. These were the sons of Hur, the firstborn of Ephrathah, the father of Bethlehem.

5Ashhur the father of Tekoa had two wives, Helah and Naarah.

6Naarah bore him Ahuzzam, Hepher, Temeni and Haahashtari. These were the sons of Naarah.

7The sons of Helah: Zereth, Zohar and Ethnan.

8Koz fathered Anub and Zobebah, and the clans of Aharhel son of Harum.

Jabez

9Jabez was more honored than his brothers. His mother called his name Jabez, saying, "Because I bore him in pain."

10Jabez called on the God of Israel, saying, "If You will indeed bless me and enlarge my border, and Your hand will be with me, and You will keep me from evil so that it does not pain me!" God granted what he asked.

More Clans of Judah

11Chelub the brother of Shuhah fathered Mehir, who was the father of Eshton.

12Eshton fathered Beth-rapha, Paseah and Tehinnah the father of Ir-nahash. These were the men of Recah.

13The sons of Kenaz: Othniel and Seraiah. The son of Othniel: Hathath.

14Meonothai fathered Ophrah, and Seraiah fathered Joab the father of Ge-harashim, for they were craftsmen.

15The sons of Caleb son of Jephunneh: Iru, Elah and Naam. The son of Elah: Kenaz.

16The sons of Jehallelel: Ziph, Ziphah, Tiria and Asarel.

17The sons of Ezrah: Jether, Mered, Epher and Jalon. She conceived and bore Miriam, Shammai and Ishbah the father of Eshtemoa.

18His Judean wife bore Jered the father of Gedor, Heber the father of Soco, and Jekuthiel the father of Zanoah. These were the sons of Bithiah the daughter of Pharaoh, whom Mered married.

19The sons of the wife of Hodiah, the sister of Naham, were the fathers of Keilah the Garmite and Eshtemoa the Maacathite.

20The sons of Shimon: Amnon, Rinnah, Ben-hanan and Tilon. The sons of Ishi: Zoheth and Ben-zoheth.

21The sons of Shelah son of Judah: Er the father of Lecah, Laadah the father of Mareshah, and the clans of the house of linen workers at Beth-ashbea;

22and Jokim, the men of Cozeba, Joash and Saraph, who ruled in Moab, and Jashubi-lehem. The records are ancient.

23These were the potters who lived at Netaim and Gederah; they lived there with the king in his work.

Simeon

24The sons of Simeon: Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah and Shaul;

25Shallum his son, Mibsam his son, Mishma his son.

26The sons of Mishma: Hammuel his son, Zaccur his son, Shimei his son.

27Shimei had sixteen sons and six daughters, but his brothers did not have many sons, and all their clan did not multiply like the sons of Judah.

28They lived in Beersheba, Moladah and Hazar-shual,

29in Bilhah, Ezem and Tolad,

30in Bethuel, Hormah and Ziklag,

31in Beth-marcaboth, Hazar-susim, Beth-biri and Shaaraim. These were their cities until David reigned.

32Their villages were Etam, Ain, Rimmon, Tochen and Ashan, five cities,

33with all their villages that were around these cities as far as Baal. These were their settlements, and they kept their own genealogy.

34Meshobab, Jamlech and Joshah son of Amaziah,

35Joel, and Jehu son of Joshibiah, son of Seraiah, son of Asiel,

36Elioenai, Jaakobah, Jeshohaiah, Asaiah, Adiel, Jesimiel and Benaiah,

37Ziza son of Shiphi, son of Allon, son of Jedaiah, son of Shimri, son of Shemaiah:

38these, mentioned by name, were leaders in their clans, and their fathers' houses increased greatly.

39They went to the entrance of Gerar, to the east side of the valley, to seek pasture for their flocks.

40There they found rich, good pasture, and the land was spacious, quiet and at peace, for those who had lived there before were of Ham.

41These, written down by name, came in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah, and struck down their tents and the Meunites who were found there, and devoted them to destruction to this day, and lived in their place, because there was pasture there for their flocks.

42Some of them, of the sons of Simeon, five hundred men, went to Mount Seir, with Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah and Uzziel, the sons of Ishi, at their head.

43They struck down the remnant of the Amalekites who had escaped, and they have lived there to this day.

Notes

  • v1 "The sons of Judah: Perez, Hezron, Carmi, Hur and Shobal" — not five brothers but descendants: Hezron is Perez's son (2:5), Hur is Hezron's grandson through Caleb (2:18–19), and Shobal is Hur's son (2:50). Sons is used of descendants.

  • v3 "These were the sons of Etam" — the Hebrew reads ve-elleh avi Eitam, and these the father of Etam, a plural with a singular that cannot both stand. The Greek has these were the sons of Etam. The text follows the Greek.

  • vv9–10 "Because I bore him in pain… so that it does not pain me" — Ya'bets and be-otsev, in pain, the same letters in another order; the word of Eve's sentence, in pain you shall bear children (Genesis 3:16). Jabez asks that the pain in his name not come on him, le-vilti otsbi. The Greek spells the name Igabes and has I bore him as a gabes, and for the end of the prayer, so as not to humble me.

  • v10 "If You will indeed bless me" — im barekh tevarakheni, an oath form with no second half: the prayer states its conditions and never says what Jabez would do. God granted what he asked.

  • v17 "She conceived and bore Miriam" — the Hebrew names no mother here; the next verse names Bithiah the daughter of Pharaoh, whom Mered married, and the order of the two verses is uncertain. Miriam here is a man of Judah, not Moses' sister.

  • v18 "Bithiah the daughter of Pharaoh" — Bityah, daughter of the LORD, the name of an Egyptian princess married into Judah. Nothing else is told of her.

  • v22 "who ruled in Moab… The records are ancient" — asher ba'alu le-Mo'av, who were masters for Moab, or who married into Moab; ba'al is used for both. The Greek has who lived in Moab. Ve-ha-devarim attiqim, an old note on old sources.

  • vv24, 28–33 "The sons of Simeon… These were their cities until David reigned" — the list of Joshua 19:2–8, where Simeon's inheritance lies within the inheritance of the sons of Judah (Joshua 19:1, 9). Genesis gives Simeon's sons as Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar and Shaul (Genesis 46:10); Numbers has Nemuel (Numbers 26:12).

  • v39 "the entrance of Gerar" — the Hebrew has Gedor, a town of Judah (v4, v18); the Greek has Gerar. Gedor and Gerar differ in one letter, d for r, and v40 says the people living there were of Ham, as the border of the Canaanites ran toward Gerar (Genesis 10:19). The text follows the Greek.

  • vv41–43 "the Meunites… the remnant of the Amalekites who had escaped" — written ha-me'inim, read ha-me'unim, the Meunites. The LORD had said, I will utterly blot out the memory of Amalek from under the heavens (Exodus 17:14); Saul and David fought them, and in Hezekiah's days the last of them are struck down.

chapters.title: Reuben, Gad and the Half-Tribe of Manasseh
chapters.html:
1 Chronicles 5

Reuben

1The sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel — he was the firstborn, but because he defiled his father's bed, his birthright was given to the sons of Joseph son of Israel, so that he is not enrolled as firstborn.

2Though Judah grew strong among his brothers and a leader came from him, the birthright belonged to Joseph —

3the sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron and Carmi.

4The sons of Joel: Shemaiah his son, Gog his son, Shimei his son,

5Micah his son, Reaiah his son, Baal his son,

6Beerah his son, whom Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria carried into exile; he was a leader of the Reubenites.

7His kinsmen by their clans, when the genealogy of their generations was recorded: the chief, Jeiel, and Zechariah,

8and Bela son of Azaz, son of Shema, son of Joel, who lived in Aroer and as far as Nebo and Baal-meon.

9To the east he lived as far as the entrance of the wilderness this side of the river Euphrates, because their livestock had multiplied in the land of Gilead.

10In the days of Saul they made war on the Hagrites, who fell into their hand, and they lived in their tents throughout all the region east of Gilead.

Gad

11The sons of Gad lived over against them in the land of Bashan as far as Salecah:

12Joel the chief, Shapham the second, Janai and Shaphat in Bashan.

13Their kinsmen by their fathers' houses: Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia and Eber, seven.

14These were the sons of Abihail son of Huri, son of Jaroah, son of Gilead, son of Michael, son of Jeshishai, son of Jahdo, son of Buz;

15Ahi son of Abdiel, son of Guni, was chief of their fathers' house.

16They lived in Gilead, in Bashan and its villages, and in all the pasturelands of Sharon to their limits.

17All of them were enrolled by genealogy in the days of Jotham king of Judah and in the days of Jeroboam king of Israel.

The War with the Hagrites

18The sons of Reuben, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh had valiant men who carried shield and sword, drew the bow and were trained for war, forty-four thousand seven hundred and sixty, ready for battle.

19They made war on the Hagrites, Jetur, Naphish and Nodab.

20They were helped against them, and the Hagrites and all who were with them were given into their hand, for they cried out to God in the battle, and He let Himself be pleaded with by them, because they trusted in Him.

21They took away their livestock: fifty thousand of their camels, two hundred and fifty thousand sheep, two thousand donkeys and a hundred thousand people.

22Many fell slain, because the war was of God. They lived in their place until the exile.

The Half-Tribe of Manasseh

23The sons of the half-tribe of Manasseh lived in the land; they were numerous from Bashan to Baal-hermon, Senir and Mount Hermon.

24These were the heads of their fathers' houses: Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah and Jahdiel, men of worth, famous men, heads of their fathers' houses.

25But they broke faith with the God of their fathers and whored after the gods of the peoples of the land, whom God had destroyed before them.

26So the God of Israel stirred up the spirit of Pul king of Assyria, the spirit of Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria, and he carried them into exile, the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh, and brought them to Halah, Habor, Hara and the river Gozan, to this day.

Notes

  • v26 and the Hebrew numbering — the Hebrew continues this chapter with fifteen more verses (5:27–41), which the English numbers 6:1–15.

  • vv1–2 "because he defiled his father's bed, his birthright was given to the sons of Joseph" — Reuben lay with Bilhah his father's secondary wife (Genesis 35:22), and Jacob's blessing took away his first place: you went up to your father's bed (Genesis 49:4). Jacob had claimed Joseph's two sons as his own, as Reuben and Simeon (Genesis 48:5). The birthright goes to Joseph, the leader to Judah: nagid, the word of David's kingship.

  • v6 "Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria" — Chronicles' spelling of Tiglath-pileser (2 Kings 15:29).

  • vv10, 19–20 "the Hagrites, Jetur, Naphish and Nodab" — Jetur and Naphish are named among the sons of Ishmael (1:31); Hagrites recalls Hagar, Ishmael's mother.

  • v20 "He let Himself be pleaded with by them" — ve-ne'tor lahem, the rare verb of Isaac's prayer for Rebekah: The LORD let Himself be pleaded with (Genesis 25:21). Here it is answered because they trusted in Him.

  • v24 "men of worth" — gibborei chayil, the fixed term.

  • v25 "whored after the gods of the peoples" — va-yiznu acharei, fixed as whore after, the words of the warning: they will whore after their gods (Exodus 34:15).

  • v26 "stirred up the spirit of Pul… the spirit of Tilgath-pilneser" — ruach, lowercase: a king's own spirit, stirred by God. Whether the two names are one king or two, the verse does not say; it repeats the spirit of for each. Kings names Pul (2 Kings 15:19) and then Tiglath-pileser, who took the land of Naphtali (2 Kings 15:29).

chapters.title: The Sons of Levi
chapters.html:
1 Chronicles 6

The High Priests

1The sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath and Merari.

2The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel.

3The children of Amram: Aaron, Moses and Miriam. The sons of Aaron: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.

4Eleazar fathered Phinehas, Phinehas fathered Abishua,

5Abishua fathered Bukki, Bukki fathered Uzzi,

6Uzzi fathered Zerahiah, Zerahiah fathered Meraioth,

7Meraioth fathered Amariah, Amariah fathered Ahitub,

8Ahitub fathered Zadok, Zadok fathered Ahimaaz,

9Ahimaaz fathered Azariah, Azariah fathered Johanan,

10and Johanan fathered Azariah — he is the one who served as priest in the house that Solomon built in Jerusalem.

11Azariah fathered Amariah, Amariah fathered Ahitub,

12Ahitub fathered Zadok, Zadok fathered Shallum,

13Shallum fathered Hilkiah, Hilkiah fathered Azariah,

14Azariah fathered Seraiah, and Seraiah fathered Jehozadak;

15and Jehozadak went into exile when the LORD carried Judah and Jerusalem into exile by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar.

The Clans of Levi

16The sons of Levi: Gershom, Kohath and Merari.

17These are the names of the sons of Gershom: Libni and Shimei.

18The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel.

19The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. These are the clans of the Levites by their fathers.

20Of Gershom: Libni his son, Jahath his son, Zimmah his son,

21Joah his son, Iddo his son, Zerah his son, Jeatherai his son.

22The sons of Kohath: Amminadab his son, Korah his son, Assir his son,

23Elkanah his son, Ebiasaph his son, Assir his son,

24Tahath his son, Uriel his son, Uzziah his son and Shaul his son.

25The sons of Elkanah: Amasai and Ahimoth,

26Elkanah his son; the sons of Elkanah: Zophai his son, Nahath his son,

27Eliab his son, Jeroham his son, Elkanah his son.

28The sons of Samuel: Joel the firstborn, and the second, Abijah.

29The sons of Merari: Mahli, Libni his son, Shimei his son, Uzzah his son,

30Shimea his son, Haggiah his son, Asaiah his son.

The Singers

31These are the men whom David put in charge of the song in the house of the LORD, after the ark came to rest.

32They ministered with song before the dwelling of the tent of meeting until Solomon built the house of the LORD in Jerusalem, and they served in their office according to their rule.

33These are the men who served, with their sons. Of the sons of the Kohathites: Heman the singer, son of Joel, son of Samuel,

34son of Elkanah, son of Jeroham, son of Eliel, son of Toah,

35son of Zuph, son of Elkanah, son of Mahath, son of Amasai,

36son of Elkanah, son of Joel, son of Azariah, son of Zephaniah,

37son of Tahath, son of Assir, son of Ebiasaph, son of Korah,

38son of Izhar, son of Kohath, son of Levi, son of Israel.

39His kinsman Asaph stood at his right hand: Asaph son of Berechiah, son of Shimea,

40son of Michael, son of Baaseiah, son of Malchijah,

41son of Ethni, son of Zerah, son of Adaiah,

42son of Ethan, son of Zimmah, son of Shimei,

43son of Jahath, son of Gershom, son of Levi.

44On the left hand were their kinsmen the sons of Merari: Ethan son of Kishi, son of Abdi, son of Malluch,

45son of Hashabiah, son of Amaziah, son of Hilkiah,

46son of Amzi, son of Bani, son of Shemer,

47son of Mahli, son of Mushi, son of Merari, son of Levi.

48Their kinsmen the Levites were appointed for all the service of the dwelling of the house of God.

Aaron and His Sons

49Aaron and his sons made offerings on the altar of burnt offering and on the altar of incense, for all the work of the most holy place, and to make atonement for Israel, according to all that Moses the servant of God had commanded.

50These are the sons of Aaron: Eleazar his son, Phinehas his son, Abishua his son,

51Bukki his son, Uzzi his son, Zerahiah his son,

52Meraioth his son, Amariah his son, Ahitub his son,

53Zadok his son, Ahimaaz his son.

54These are their dwelling places by their encampments within their borders. To the sons of Aaron, of the clan of the Kohathites, for the lot fell to them,

55they gave Hebron in the land of Judah with its pasture lands around it.

56But the fields of the town and its villages they gave to Caleb son of Jephunneh.

57To the sons of Aaron they gave the towns of refuge: Hebron, Libnah with its pasture lands, Jattir, Eshtemoa with its pasture lands,

58Hilen with its pasture lands, Debir with its pasture lands,

59Ashan with its pasture lands and Beth-shemesh with its pasture lands;

60and from the tribe of Benjamin, Geba with its pasture lands, Alemeth with its pasture lands and Anathoth with its pasture lands. All their towns throughout their clans were thirteen towns.

61To the rest of the sons of Kohath were given by lot ten towns from the clan of the tribe, from the half-tribe, the half of Manasseh.

62To the sons of Gershom, by their clans, were given thirteen towns from the tribe of Issachar, the tribe of Asher, the tribe of Naphtali and the tribe of Manasseh in Bashan.

64So the sons of Israel gave the Levites the towns with their pasture lands.

65They gave by lot, from the tribe of the sons of Judah, the tribe of the sons of Simeon and the tribe of the sons of Benjamin, these towns that are mentioned by name.

66Some of the clans of the sons of Kohath had towns of their territory from the tribe of Ephraim.

67They gave them the towns of refuge: Shechem with its pasture lands in the hill country of Ephraim, Gezer with its pasture lands,

68Jokmeam with its pasture lands, Beth-horon with its pasture lands,

69Aijalon with its pasture lands and Gath-rimmon with its pasture lands;

70and from the half-tribe of Manasseh, Aner with its pasture lands and Bileam with its pasture lands, for the clan of the rest of the sons of Kohath.

72from the tribe of Issachar, Kedesh with its pasture lands, Daberath with its pasture lands,

73Ramoth with its pasture lands and Anem with its pasture lands;

74from the tribe of Asher, Mashal with its pasture lands, Abdon with its pasture lands,

75Hukok with its pasture lands and Rehob with its pasture lands;

76and from the tribe of Naphtali, Kedesh in Galilee with its pasture lands, Hammon with its pasture lands and Kiriathaim with its pasture lands.

79Kedemoth with its pasture lands and Mephaath with its pasture lands;

80and from the tribe of Gad, Ramoth in Gilead with its pasture lands, Mahanaim with its pasture lands,

81Heshbon with its pasture lands and Jazer with its pasture lands.

Notes

  • vv1–81 in the Hebrew — the Hebrew numbers vv1–15 as 5:27–41 and vv16–81 as 6:1–66.

  • vv1–15 "Eleazar fathered Phinehas… Jehozadak went into exile" — the line of high priests from Aaron to the exile. Ezra traces himself through the same names, Ezra son of Seraiah, son of Azariah, son of Hilkiah (Ezra 7:1). In v10 the note he is the one who served as priest in the house that Solomon built stands against the second Azariah; Kings names Azariah son of Zadok as Solomon's priest (1 Kings 4:2).

  • vv1, 16 "Gershon… Gershom" — the Hebrew spells Levi's son Gershon in v1 and Gershom, the name of Moses' son, from v16 on.

  • v28 "Joel the firstborn, and the second, Abijah" — the Hebrew reads ha-bekhor ve-sheni va-Aviyyah, the firstborn and the second and Abijah, with no name for the firstborn; the scribes' vowels and the Greek read ve-sheni as a name, Vashni. This chapter itself names Samuel's son Joel (v33), and Samuel's book says the name of his firstborn son was Joel, and the name of his second, Abijah (1 Samuel 8:2). The text follows them.

  • vv22–28, 33–38 "Elkanah… Samuel" — Samuel counted among the Levites, of Korah's line. Samuel's own book calls his father Elkanah an Ephrathite from the hill country of Ephraim (1 Samuel 1:1); Chronicles lists the family among the Levites.

  • vv31–32 "David put in charge of the song… after the ark came to rest" — the singers' service begins when the ark comes to Jerusalem (chapters 15–16). Heman, Asaph and Ethan (vv33, 39, 44) are names from the headings of the Psalms: Asaph (Psalms 50, 73–83), Heman the Ezrahite (Psalm 88), Ethan the Ezrahite (Psalm 89).

  • v49 "to make atonement for Israel… Moses the servant of God" — le-khapper, the priests' work set apart from the Levites' service in v48.

  • vv54–81 "the towns of the Levites" — the list of Joshua 21, with many differences in names and some towns missing. Joshua names thirteen towns for Aaron's sons (Joshua 21:13–19); Chronicles counts thirteen (v60) but names eleven, without Juttah and Gibeon, and has Ashan for Ain and Alemeth for Almon.

  • v57 "the towns of refuge: Hebron, Libnah…" — the Hebrew has the plural, towns of refuge, before a list in which only Hebron was one; Joshua has Hebron, the town of refuge for the one who killed (Joshua 21:13). The text keeps the Hebrew.

  • v61 "from the clan of the tribe, from the half-tribe, the half of Manasseh" — Joshua says from the clans of the tribe of Ephraim, from the tribe of Dan and from the half-tribe of Manasseh (Joshua 21:5). The Hebrew of Chronicles lacks Ephraim and Dan, and the phrase breaks off; the text keeps it as it stands.

chapters.title: Issachar, Benjamin, Naphtali, Manasseh, Ephraim and Asher
chapters.html:
1 Chronicles 7

Issachar

1The sons of Issachar: Tola, Puah, Jashub and Shimron, four.

2The sons of Tola: Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Ibsam and Shemuel, heads of their fathers' houses, of Tola, men of worth in their generations; their number in the days of David was twenty-two thousand six hundred.

3The son of Uzzi: Izrahiah. The sons of Izrahiah: Michael, Obadiah, Joel and Isshiah, five, all of them chiefs.

4With them, by their generations, by their fathers' houses, were troops of the army for war, thirty-six thousand, for they had many wives and sons.

5Their kinsmen of all the clans of Issachar were men of worth, eighty-seven thousand, all enrolled by genealogy.

Benjamin

6The sons of Benjamin: Bela, Becher and Jediael, three.

7The sons of Bela: Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth and Iri, five, heads of fathers' houses, men of worth; and their enrollment was twenty-two thousand thirty-four.

8The sons of Becher: Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth and Alemeth. All these were the sons of Becher.

9Their enrollment by their generations, heads of their fathers' houses, men of worth, was twenty thousand two hundred.

10The son of Jediael: Bilhan. The sons of Bilhan: Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish and Ahishahar.

11All these were the sons of Jediael, by heads of fathers' houses, men of worth, seventeen thousand two hundred, ready to go out in the army for war.

12Shuppim and Huppim were the sons of Ir; Hushim the sons of Aher.

Naphtali

13The sons of Naphtali: Jahziel, Guni, Jezer and Shallum, the sons of Bilhah.

Manasseh

14The sons of Manasseh: Asriel, whom his Aramean secondary wife bore; she bore Machir the father of Gilead.

15Machir took a wife for Huppim and for Shuppim. The name of his sister was Maacah. The name of the second was Zelophehad, and Zelophehad had daughters.

16Maacah the wife of Machir bore a son, and she called his name Peresh. The name of his brother was Sheresh, and his sons were Ulam and Rakem.

17The son of Ulam: Bedan. These were the sons of Gilead son of Machir, son of Manasseh.

18His sister Hammolecheth bore Ishhod, Abiezer and Mahlah.

19The sons of Shemida were Ahian, Shechem, Likhi and Aniam.

Ephraim

20The sons of Ephraim: Shuthelah, Bered his son, Tahath his son, Eleadah his son, Tahath his son,

21Zabad his son, Shuthelah his son, and Ezer and Elead, whom the men of Gath who were born in the land killed, because they came down to take their livestock.

22Ephraim their father mourned many days, and his brothers came to comfort him.

23Then he went in to his wife, and she conceived and bore a son, and he called his name Beriah, because it was in evil that it happened to his house.

24His daughter was Sheerah, who built Lower and Upper Beth-horon, and Uzzen-sheerah.

25Rephah was his son, Resheph, Telah his son, Tahan his son,

26Ladan his son, Ammihud his son, Elishama his son,

27Nun his son, Joshua his son.

28Their holdings and settlements were Bethel and its villages, and to the east Naaran, and to the west Gezer and its villages, Shechem and its villages, as far as Ayyah and its villages;

29and along the borders of the sons of Manasseh, Beth-shean and its villages, Taanach and its villages, Megiddo and its villages, Dor and its villages. In these lived the sons of Joseph son of Israel.

Asher

30The sons of Asher: Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi and Beriah, and their sister Serah.

31The sons of Beriah: Heber and Malchiel, who was the father of Birzaith.

32Heber fathered Japhlet, Shomer, Hotham and their sister Shua.

33The sons of Japhlet: Pasach, Bimhal and Ashvath. These were the sons of Japhlet.

34The sons of Shemer: Ahi, Rohgah, Hubbah and Aram.

35The sons of Helem his brother: Zophah, Imna, Shelesh and Amal.

36The sons of Zophah: Suah, Harnepher, Shual, Beri, Imrah,

37Bezer, Hod, Shamma, Shilshah, Ithran and Beera.

38The sons of Jether: Jephunneh, Pispa and Ara.

39The sons of Ulla: Arah, Hanniel and Rizia.

40All these were the sons of Asher, heads of fathers' houses, choice men of worth, chiefs of the leaders. Their number enrolled by genealogy for service in war was twenty-six thousand men.

Notes

  • vv1–40 "Issachar… Asher" — six tribes in one chapter, with numbers in the days of David (v2) like those of a muster. Zebulun and Dan have no genealogy in chapters 2–8.

  • v1 "Jashub" — written Yashiv, read Yashuv; Genesis has Job (Genesis 46:13) and Numbers Jashub (Numbers 26:24).

  • vv2, 5, 7, 9, 11, 40 "men of worth" — gibborei chayil, the fixed term, here in a count of fighting men.

  • v6 "Bela, Becher and Jediael" — Genesis gives Benjamin ten sons, Bela, Becher, Ashbel, Gera, Naaman, Ehi, Rosh, Muppim, Huppim and Ard (Genesis 46:21), and the next chapter has Bela his firstborn, Ashbel the second, Aharah the third (8:1). The lists do not agree.

  • v12 "Hushim the sons of Aher" — Acher is also the word another. Genesis names Hushim as the son of Dan (Genesis 46:23). The Greek has the sons of Raom, his son Aer.

  • vv14–15 "Asriel, whom his Aramean secondary wife bore… Machir took a wife for Huppim and for Shuppim" — the Hebrew of these two verses does not run smoothly: the subject of bore in v14 is unclear, and in v15 his sister and the second have nothing to refer back to. Zelophehad had daughters: the five daughters who asked Moses for their father's inheritance (Numbers 27:1). The text keeps the Hebrew.

  • v18 "Abiezer" — the clan of Gideon, Joash the Abiezrite (Judges 6:11).

  • vv21–23 "the men of Gath… killed… Ephraim their father mourned many days… Beriah" — the words of Jacob's grief: mourned for his son many days. All his sons and all his daughters rose to comfort him (Genesis 37:34–35). Beri'ah is named for be-ra'ah, in evil.

  • v24 "Sheerah, who built Lower and Upper Beth-horon" — the only woman in these lists said to have built towns.

  • vv25–27 "Nun his son, Joshua his son" — Joshua son of Nun, here at the end of Ephraim's line. Written Birzoth, read Birzaith (v31); written ve-Rohagah, read ve-Rohgah, and written Yechubbah, read ve-Chubbah (v34).

1 Chronicles 8

The Sons of Benjamin

1Benjamin fathered Bela his firstborn, Ashbel the second, Aharah the third,

2Nohah the fourth and Rapha the fifth.

3Bela had sons: Addar, Gera, Abihud,

4Abishua, Naaman, Ahoah,

5Gera, Shephuphan and Huram.

6These are the sons of Ehud — they were heads of fathers' houses of the inhabitants of Geba, and they carried them into exile to Manahath:

7Naaman, Ahijah and Gera — he carried them into exile — and he fathered Uzza and Ahihud.

8Shaharaim fathered sons in the country of Moab after he had sent away Hushim and Baara his wives.

9By Hodesh his wife he fathered Jobab, Zibia, Mesha, Malcam,

10Jeuz, Sachia and Mirmah. These were his sons, heads of fathers' houses.

11By Hushim he fathered Abitub and Elpaal.

12The sons of Elpaal: Eber, Misham and Shemed, who built Ono and Lod with its villages,

13and Beriah and Shema, who were heads of fathers' houses of the inhabitants of Aijalon, who put to flight the inhabitants of Gath;

14and Ahio, Shashak and Jeremoth.

15Zebadiah, Arad, Eder,

23Abdon, Zichri, Hanan,

29In Gibeon lived the father of Gibeon, and the name of his wife was Maacah.

30His firstborn son was Abdon, then Zur, Kish, Baal, Nadab,

31Gedor, Ahio and Zecher.

32Mikloth fathered Shimeah. They also lived opposite their kinsmen in Jerusalem, with their kinsmen.

33Ner fathered Kish, Kish fathered Saul, and Saul fathered Jonathan, Malchi-shua, Abinadab and Eshbaal.

38Azel had six sons, and these are their names: Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah and Hanan. All these were the sons of Azel.

39The sons of Eshek his brother: Ulam his firstborn, Jeush the second and Eliphelet the third.

  • vv1–2 "Bela his firstborn, Ashbel the second, Aharah the third" — the third list of Benjamin's sons, after Genesis 46:21 and 7:6, and it agrees with neither.

  • v8 "after he had sent away Hushim and Baara his wives" — shilcho otam, his sending them away, the verb of divorce: he writes her a certificate of divorce, puts it in her hand and sends her out of his house (Deuteronomy 24:1).

  • vv30, 33 "Kish, Baal, Nadab… Ner fathered Kish" — the list in 9:36 has Ner between Baal and Nadab; here he is missing from the sons, though v33 names him. The Greek here also lacks him. Samuel says Kish was the father of Saul, and Ner the father of Abner was the son of Abiel (1 Samuel 14:51).

  • v33 "Saul fathered Jonathan, Malchi-shua, Abinadab and Eshbaal" — Samuel calls the last son Ish-bosheth (2 Samuel 2:8): baal, lord, the name of the god, replaced by bosheth, shame, as Jeremiah speaks of altars to the shame, altars to burn incense to Baal (Jeremiah 11:13).   • v34 "Merib-baal" — the son of Jonathan whom Samuel calls Mephibosheth (2 Samuel 4:4), with the same change; his son Mica (2 Samuel 9:12).

  • v38 "Azrikam, Bocheru" — the scribes' vowels read Bokheru as a name, which makes the six sons; the same letters could be read bekhoro, his firstborn, as Ulam his firstborn in v39, and then five names would stand for six. The text follows the vowels. Written Peniel, read Penuel (v25).

  • v40 "archers" — dorkhei qeshet, benders of the bow. Judges counts seven hundred left-handed Benjaminites who could sling a stone at a hair (Judges 20:16).

chapters.title: Those Who Lived in Jerusalem
chapters.html:
1 Chronicles 9

The Returned Exiles

1So all Israel was enrolled by genealogy, and they are written in the book of the kings of Israel. Judah was carried into exile to Babylon because of their unfaithfulness.

2The first to live again in their holdings in their towns were Israel, the priests, the Levites and the temple servants.

3In Jerusalem lived some of the sons of Judah, of the sons of Benjamin, and of the sons of Ephraim and Manasseh:

4Uthai son of Ammihud, son of Omri, son of Imri, son of Bani, of the sons of Perez son of Judah.

5Of the Shilonites: Asaiah the firstborn and his sons.

6Of the sons of Zerah: Jeuel and their kinsmen, six hundred and ninety.

7Of the sons of Benjamin: Sallu son of Meshullam, son of Hodaviah, son of Hassenuah,

8Ibneiah son of Jeroham, Elah son of Uzzi, son of Michri, and Meshullam son of Shephatiah, son of Reuel, son of Ibnijah,

9and their kinsmen by their generations, nine hundred and fifty-six. All these men were heads of fathers' houses by their fathers' houses.

The Priests

10Of the priests: Jedaiah, Jehoiarib, Jachin,

11and Azariah son of Hilkiah, son of Meshullam, son of Zadok, son of Meraioth, son of Ahitub, the leader of the house of God;

12and Adaiah son of Jeroham, son of Pashhur, son of Malchijah, and Maasai son of Adiel, son of Jahzerah, son of Meshullam, son of Meshillemith, son of Immer,

13and their kinsmen, heads of their fathers' houses, a thousand seven hundred and sixty, men of worth for the work of the service of the house of God.

The Levites

14Of the Levites: Shemaiah son of Hasshub, son of Azrikam, son of Hashabiah, of the sons of Merari;

15Bakbakkar, Heresh, Galal, and Mattaniah son of Mica, son of Zichri, son of Asaph;

16Obadiah son of Shemaiah, son of Galal, son of Jeduthun; and Berechiah son of Asa, son of Elkanah, who lived in the villages of the Netophathites.

The Gatekeepers

17The gatekeepers: Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, Ahiman and their kinsmen; Shallum was the chief,

18stationed until now at the king's gate on the east. These were the gatekeepers of the camps of the sons of Levi.

19Shallum son of Kore, son of Ebiasaph, son of Korah, and his kinsmen of his father's house, the Korahites, were over the work of the service, keepers of the thresholds of the tent, as their fathers had been over the camp of the LORD, keepers of the entrance.

20Phinehas son of Eleazar was the leader over them in time past; the LORD was with him.

21Zechariah son of Meshelemiah was gatekeeper at the entrance of the tent of meeting.

22All these, chosen to be gatekeepers at the thresholds, were two hundred and twelve. They were enrolled by genealogy in their villages. David and Samuel the seer appointed them in their trust.

23So they and their sons were in charge of the gates of the house of the LORD, the house of the tent, as guards.

24The gatekeepers were on the four sides, east, west, north and south.

25Their kinsmen in their villages were to come in every seven days, from time to time, to be with them,

26for the four chief gatekeepers, who were Levites, were in an office of trust, and they were over the chambers and the treasuries of the house of God.

27They spent the night around the house of God, for the watch was theirs, and they were in charge of opening it morning by morning.

28Some of them were in charge of the vessels of the service, for they brought them in by count and took them out by count.

29Some of them were appointed over the furniture and over all the holy vessels, and over the fine flour, the wine, the oil, the frankincense and the spices.

30Some of the sons of the priests mixed the ointment of the spices.

31Mattithiah, one of the Levites, the firstborn of Shallum the Korahite, was in an office of trust over the making of the flat cakes.

32Some of their kinsmen of the sons of the Kohathites were over the rows of bread, to prepare them every Sabbath.

33These were the singers, heads of fathers' houses of the Levites, in the chambers, free from other duty, for they were on duty day and night.

34These were heads of fathers' houses of the Levites by their generations, chiefs. These lived in Jerusalem.

The House of Saul Again

35In Gibeon lived the father of Gibeon, Jeiel, and the name of his wife was Maacah.

36His firstborn son was Abdon, then Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, Nadab,

37Gedor, Ahio, Zechariah and Mikloth.

38Mikloth fathered Shimeam. They also lived opposite their kinsmen in Jerusalem, with their kinsmen.

39Ner fathered Kish, Kish fathered Saul, and Saul fathered Jonathan, Malchi-shua, Abinadab and Eshbaal.

40The son of Jonathan was Merib-baal, and Meri-baal fathered Micah.

41The sons of Micah: Pithon, Melech and Tahrea.

42Ahaz fathered Jarah, and Jarah fathered Alemeth, Azmaveth and Zimri. Zimri fathered Moza.

43Moza fathered Binea; Rephaiah was his son, Eleasah his son, Azel his son.

44Azel had six sons, and these are their names: Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah and Hanan. These were the sons of Azel.

Notes

  • v1 "they are written in the book of the kings of Israel. Judah was carried into exile" — the Hebrew can also be divided the book of the kings of Israel and Judah. They were carried into exile; the Greek reads it so. The text follows the accents of the Hebrew. Be-ma'alam, in their unfaithfulness, the word of Achar, who broke faith (2:7).

  • vv2–34 and Nehemiah 11 — the same list, with many differences, stands in Nehemiah 11:3–19, as the people who settled in Jerusalem after the exile. There the chief priest is Seraiah son of Hilkiah (Nehemiah 11:11) where this list has Azariah son of Hilkiah (v11).

  • v2 "the temple servants" — ha-netinim, the given ones. The Levites themselves were wholly given to Aaron (Numbers 3:9), and Joshua gave the Gibeonites to be woodcutters and water carriers for the altar of the LORD (Joshua 9:27).

  • v4 "son of Bani" — written Binyamin, Benjamin, read Bani. The text follows the read form.

  • v20 "Phinehas son of Eleazar… the LORD was with him" — the priest who was given a covenant of lasting priesthood, because he was jealous for his God (Numbers 25:13).

  • v22 "David and Samuel the seer appointed them" — ha-ro'eh, the seer, the old title: the one who is now called a prophet was formerly called a seer (1 Samuel 9:9).

  • v32 "the rows of bread" — lechem ha-ma'arakhet, the bread of the row, set in two rows, six to a row, on the pure table before the LORD and renewed every sabbath day (Leviticus 24:6–8).

  • v33 "free from other duty" — written petirim, read peturim, the same word.

  • vv35–44 "In Gibeon lived the father of Gibeon, Jeiel" — the list of 8:29–38 again, here as the bridge to Saul's death in chapter 10. This copy has Jeiel and Ner where 8:29–30 lacks them, and lacks Ahaz among Micah's sons (v41) where 8:35 has him. Written Je'uel, read Je'iel (v35).

  • v40 "Merib-baal, and Meri-baal" — two spellings of the one name in one verse.

chapters.title: The Death of Saul
chapters.html:
1 Chronicles 10

Mount Gilboa

1The Philistines fought against Israel, and the men of Israel fled before the Philistines and fell slain on Mount Gilboa.

2The Philistines closed in on Saul and his sons, and the Philistines struck down Jonathan, Abinadab and Malchi-shua, the sons of Saul.

3The battle pressed hard against Saul. The archers found him, and he was wounded by the archers.

4Saul said to his armor-bearer, "Draw your sword and run me through with it, or these uncircumcised will come and abuse me." But his armor-bearer would not, for he was greatly afraid. So Saul took the sword and fell on it.

5When his armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead, he also fell on the sword and died.

6So Saul died, and his three sons, and all his house died together.

7When all the men of Israel who were in the valley saw that the army had fled and that Saul and his sons were dead, they abandoned their towns and fled, and the Philistines came and lived in them.

8And it came to pass the next day, when the Philistines came to strip the slain, that they found Saul and his sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.

9They stripped him and took his head and his armor, and sent them throughout the land of the Philistines to carry the news to their idols and to the people.

10They put his armor in the house of their gods and fastened his skull in the house of Dagon.

11When all Jabesh-gilead heard all that the Philistines had done to Saul,

12all the men of valor arose and took the body of Saul and the bodies of his sons and brought them to Jabesh. They buried their bones under the oak in Jabesh, and they fasted seven days.

Why Saul Died

13So Saul died for his unfaithfulness with which he broke faith with the LORD, because of the word of the LORD that he did not keep, and also because he asked a ghost, to inquire of it,

14and did not inquire of the LORD. So He put him to death and turned the kingdom over to David son of Jesse.

Notes

  • vv1–12 and 1 Samuel 31 — Chronicles begins its story with Saul's last battle, told almost word for word as in 1 Samuel 31. Chronicles tells no other story of Saul's reign.

  • v3 "he was wounded by the archers" — va-yachel, he was wounded, or he writhed; Samuel has va-yachel me'od, he was in great anguish (1 Samuel 31:3).

  • v6 "all his house died together" — Samuel has his armor-bearer and all his men (1 Samuel 31:6). Saul's son Ish-bosheth reigned after him for two years (2 Samuel 2:10); Chronicles does not mention him.

  • v10 "fastened his skull in the house of Dagon" — Samuel has the armor in the house of the Ashtaroth and the body on the wall of Beth-shan (1 Samuel 31:10). Dagon is the god whose image fell before the ark (1 Samuel 5:3–4).

  • v12 "the bodies… under the oak" — gufat, body, found only here; Samuel has geviyyat and the tamarisk tree (1 Samuel 31:12–13). Chronicles also leaves out the burning of the bodies.

  • vv13–14 "his unfaithfulness… the word of the LORD that he did not keep" — be-ma'alo asher ma'al, the word of Achar's sin (2:7) and of Judah's exile (9:1). Samuel told Saul, You have not kept the command of the LORD your God (1 Samuel 13:13).

  • vv13–14 "he asked a ghost… and did not inquire of the LORD" — sho'el ba-ov, the medium of En-dor (1 Samuel 28:7); ov, fixed as ghost. Samuel says that Saul inquired of the LORD, but the LORD did not answer him (1 Samuel 28:6). Sho'el, asking, is the verb of Saul's own name, Sha'ul, asked.

  • v14 "So He put him to death" — Saul fell on his own sword (v4), and the same death is here the LORD's act.

chapters.title: David King over All Israel
chapters.html:
1 Chronicles 11

David Anointed at Hebron

1Then all Israel gathered to David at Hebron and said, "We are your bone and your flesh.

2In times past, even when Saul was king, it was you who led Israel out and brought them in. The LORD your God said to you, 'You shall shepherd My people Israel, and you shall be leader over My people Israel.'"

3So all the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron, and David made a covenant with them at Hebron before the LORD, and they anointed David king over Israel, according to the word of the LORD by Samuel.

Jerusalem Taken

4David and all Israel went to Jerusalem, that is, Jebus, where the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land, were.

5The inhabitants of Jebus said to David, "You will not come in here." But David took the stronghold of Zion, that is, the City of David.

6David said, "Whoever strikes the Jebusites first shall be chief and commander." Joab son of Zeruiah went up first, and he became chief.

7David lived in the stronghold; therefore they called it the City of David.

8He built the city all around, from the Millo to the surrounding wall, and Joab restored the rest of the city.

9David grew greater and greater, and the LORD of hosts was with him.

David's Mighty Men

10These are the chiefs of David's mighty men, who held strongly with him in his kingdom, with all Israel, to make him king, according to the word of the LORD concerning Israel.

11This is the list of David's mighty men: Jashobeam son of Hachmoni, chief of the officers. He wielded his spear against three hundred, whom he killed at one time.

12After him was Eleazar son of Dodo the Ahohite; he was one of the three mighty men.

13He was with David at Pas-dammim when the Philistines were gathered there for battle. There was a plot of ground full of barley, and the people fled from the Philistines.

14But they took their stand in the middle of the plot, defended it and struck down the Philistines, and the LORD saved them with a great victory.

15Three of the thirty chiefs went down to the rock, to David at the cave of Adullam, while the army of the Philistines was camped in the Valley of Rephaim.

16David was then in the stronghold, and the Philistine garrison was then at Bethlehem.

17David longed and said, "If only someone would give me water to drink from the well of Bethlehem that is by the gate!"

18So the three broke through the camp of the Philistines, drew water from the well of Bethlehem that was by the gate, and carried it and brought it to David. But David would not drink it; he poured it out to the LORD.

19He said, "Far be it from me before my God that I should do this. Shall I drink the blood of these men who went at the risk of their lives? For at the risk of their lives they brought it." So he would not drink it. These things the three mighty men did.

20Abishai, the brother of Joab, was chief of the Three. He wielded his spear against three hundred, whom he killed, and won a name among the Three.

21Of the Three he was doubly honored, and he became their commander, but he did not attain to the Three.

22Benaiah son of Jehoiada was the son of a man of valor from Kabzeel, great in deeds. He struck down the two Ariels of Moab. He also went down and struck down a lion inside a pit on a day of snow.

The Thirty

26The mighty men of the armies were Asahel the brother of Joab, Elhanan son of Dodo of Bethlehem,

27Shammoth the Harorite, Helez the Pelonite,

28Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite, Abiezer the Anathothite,

29Sibbecai the Hushathite, Ilai the Ahohite,

30Maharai the Netophathite, Heled son of Baanah the Netophathite,

31Ithai son of Ribai from Gibeah of the sons of Benjamin, Benaiah the Pirathonite,

32Hurai of the brooks of Gaash, Abiel the Arbathite,

33Azmaveth the Baharumite, Eliahba the Shaalbonite,

34the sons of Hashem the Gizonite, Jonathan son of Shagee the Hararite,

35Ahiam son of Sachar the Hararite, Eliphal son of Ur,

36Hepher the Mecherathite, Ahijah the Pelonite,

37Hezro the Carmelite, Naarai son of Ezbai,

38Joel the brother of Nathan, Mibhar son of Hagri,

39Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai the Berothite, the armor-bearer of Joab son of Zeruiah,

40Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite,

41Uriah the Hittite, Zabad son of Ahlai,

42Adina son of Shiza the Reubenite, a chief of the Reubenites, and thirty with him,

43Hanan son of Maacah, Joshaphat the Mithnite,

44Uzzia the Ashterathite, Shama and Jeiel the sons of Hotham the Aroerite,

45Jediael son of Shimri, and Joha his brother, the Tizite,

46Eliel the Mahavite, Jeribai and Joshaviah the sons of Elnaam, Ithmah the Moabite,

  • v23 "five cubits tall… a spear like a weaver's beam" — Samuel says only a man of great stature; the weaver's beam is the spear-shaft of Goliath (1 Samuel 17:7).

chapters.title: Those Who Came to David
chapters.html:
1 Chronicles 12

At Ziklag

1These are the men who came to David at Ziklag while he was still kept away from Saul son of Kish. They were among the mighty men who helped him in war.

2They were armed with bows and could use both the right hand and the left in slinging stones and shooting arrows with the bow. They were of Saul's kinsmen, from Benjamin:

3the chief Ahiezer, then Joash, the sons of Shemaah the Gibeathite; Jeziel and Pelet the sons of Azmaveth; Beracah, Jehu the Anathothite,

4Ishmaiah the Gibeonite, a mighty man among the Thirty and over the Thirty; Jeremiah, Jahaziel, Johanan, Jozabad the Gederathite,

5Eluzai, Jerimoth, Bealiah, Shemariah, Shephatiah the Haruphite,

6Elkanah, Isshiah, Azarel, Joezer and Jashobeam, the Korahites,

7and Joelah and Zebadiah the sons of Jeroham of Gedor.

From Gad

8From the Gadites there went over to David at the stronghold in the wilderness men of valor, men trained for war, who could handle shield and spear, whose faces were like the faces of lions, and who were as swift as gazelles on the mountains:

9Ezer the chief, Obadiah the second, Eliab the third,

10Mishmannah the fourth, Jeremiah the fifth,

11Attai the sixth, Eliel the seventh,

12Johanan the eighth, Elzabad the ninth,

13Jeremiah the tenth, Machbannai the eleventh.

14These of the sons of Gad were heads of the army; the least was a match for a hundred, and the greatest for a thousand.

15These are the men who crossed the Jordan in the first month, when it was overflowing all its banks, and put to flight all those in the valleys, to the east and to the west.

From Benjamin and Judah

16Some of the sons of Benjamin and Judah came to the stronghold to David.

17David went out to meet them and said to them, "If you have come to me in peace to help me, my heart will be joined to you; but if you have come to betray me to my enemies, though there is no violence in my hands, may the God of our fathers see and rebuke you."

18Then the spirit clothed Amasai, the chief of the officers:
"We are yours, O David,
and with you, O son of Jesse!
Peace, peace to you,
and peace to your helpers,
for your God helps you."
Then David received them and made them officers of the troop.

From Manasseh

19Some from Manasseh deserted to David when he came with the Philistines to battle against Saul. But he did not help them, for the lords of the Philistines took counsel and sent him away, saying, "At the cost of our heads he will desert to his master Saul."

20As he went to Ziklag, these deserted to him from Manasseh: Adnah, Jozabad, Jediael, Michael, Jozabad, Elihu and Zillethai, chiefs of thousands of Manasseh.

21They helped David against the band of raiders, for they were all men of worth, and they became commanders in the army.

22Day by day men came to David to help him, until there was a great camp, like the camp of God.

The Army at Hebron

23These are the numbers of the chiefs of those armed for war who came to David at Hebron to turn the kingdom of Saul over to him, according to the word of the LORD.

24The sons of Judah who carried shield and spear, six thousand eight hundred, armed for war.

25Of the sons of Simeon, men of worth for war, seven thousand one hundred.

26Of the sons of Levi, four thousand six hundred.

27Jehoiada, the leader of the house of Aaron, and with him three thousand seven hundred,

28and Zadok, a young man of worth, and his father's house, twenty-two commanders.

29Of the sons of Benjamin, Saul's kinsmen, three thousand, for until then most of them had kept their allegiance to the house of Saul.

30Of the sons of Ephraim, twenty thousand eight hundred, men of worth, famous men in their fathers' houses.

31Of the half-tribe of Manasseh, eighteen thousand, who were designated by name to come and make David king.

32Of the sons of Issachar, men who understood the times, to know what Israel ought to do, two hundred chiefs, and all their kinsmen under their command.

33Of Zebulun, fifty thousand ready for battle, armed for war with all the weapons of war, to help with an undivided heart.

34Of Naphtali, a thousand commanders, and with them thirty-seven thousand with shield and spear.

35Of the Danites, twenty-eight thousand six hundred armed for war.

36Of Asher, forty thousand ready for battle, armed for war.

37From beyond the Jordan, of the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh, a hundred and twenty thousand with all the weapons of war.

38All these men of war, ready in battle order, came to Hebron with a whole heart to make David king over all Israel, and all the rest of Israel too were of one heart to make David king.

39They were there with David three days, eating and drinking, for their kinsmen had provided for them.

40Those who were near them also, as far as Issachar, Zebulun and Naphtali, brought food on donkeys, camels, mules and oxen: provisions of flour, cakes of figs, clusters of raisins, wine, oil, cattle and sheep in abundance, for there was joy in Israel.

Notes

  • vv1–40 in the Hebrew — the Hebrew divides v4 in two (4–5) and numbers vv5–40 as 6–41.

  • v1 "while he was still kept away from Saul" — atsur, shut in, held back: David's time among the Philistines, when Achish gave him Ziklag (1 Samuel 27:6).

  • v2 "both the right hand and the left… from Benjamin" — Benjamin, son of the right hand, sends men who use either hand; Judges counts seven hundred left-handed Benjaminites who could sling a stone at a hair (Judges 20:16).

  • v8 "faces like the faces of lions… as swift as gazelles on the mountains" — Asahel was as swift of foot as a gazelle in the field (2 Samuel 2:18).

  • v15 "crossed the Jordan in the first month, when it was overflowing all its banks" — the flood season of Joshua's crossing: the Jordan overflows all its banks all the days of harvest (Joshua 3:15). Written gidyotav, read gedotav, its banks.

  • v18 "Then the spirit clothed Amasai" — ve-ruach lavshah et Amasai, the verb of The Spirit of the LORD clothed Gideon (Judges 6:34). Here the Hebrew says only ruach, spirit, without of God or of the LORD, and it stays lowercase. Written ha-sheloshim, the thirty, read ha-shalishim, the officers.

  • v19 "At the cost of our heads he will desert to his master Saul" — the Philistine commanders in Samuel: how could this man win back his lord's favor? Would it not be with the heads of these men? (1 Samuel 29:4).

  • v22 "a great camp, like the camp of God" — ke-machaneh Elohim, Jacob's words when the messengers of God met him: This is God's camp (Genesis 32:2).

  • v32 "men who understood the times, to know what Israel ought to do" — yode'ei vinah la-ittim. Issachar alone is counted by the understanding of its chiefs, with no number of fighting men.

  • vv33, 38 "an undivided heart… a whole heart… one heart" — be-lo lev va-lev, without a heart and a heart; then be-levav shalem and lev echad. The chapter ends in a single heart and joy in Israel (v40).

chapters.title: The Ark and Uzza
chapters.html:
1 Chronicles 13

David Consults the Assembly

1David consulted with the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, with every leader.

2David said to all the assembly of Israel, "If it seems good to you, and if it is from the LORD our God, let us send word far and wide to our kinsmen who remain in all the lands of Israel, and with them to the priests and Levites in their towns that have pasture lands, that they may gather to us.

3Then let us bring back the ark of our God to us, for we did not seek it in the days of Saul."

4All the assembly agreed to do so, for the thing was right in the eyes of all the people.

The New Cart

5So David gathered all Israel, from the Shihor of Egypt to Lebo-hamath, to bring the ark of God from Kiriath-jearim.

6David and all Israel went up to Baalah, that is, Kiriath-jearim, which belongs to Judah, to bring up from there the ark of God, the LORD, who is enthroned on the cherubim, which is called by the name.

7They carried the ark of God on a new cart from the house of Abinadab, and Uzza and Ahio were driving the cart.

8David and all Israel were celebrating before God with all their might, with songs, lyres, harps, tambourines, cymbals and trumpets.

9When they came to the threshing floor of Chidon, Uzza put out his hand to take hold of the ark, for the oxen stumbled.

10The anger of the LORD burned against Uzza, and He struck him down because he put out his hand to the ark, and he died there before God.

11David was angry because the LORD had broken out against Uzza, and that place is called Perez-uzza to this day.

12David was afraid of God that day and said, "How can I bring the ark of God home to me?"

13So David did not take the ark home to himself into the City of David, but turned it aside to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.

14The ark of God remained with the household of Obed-edom in his house three months, and the LORD blessed the household of Obed-edom and all that he had.

Notes

  • vv1–4 "If it seems good to you, and if it is from the LORD our God" — in Samuel David simply gathers the chosen men of Israel and goes (2 Samuel 6:1–2); in Chronicles the whole assembly agrees first.

  • vv2, 11 "let us send word far and wide… the LORD had broken out against Uzza" — nifretsah, let us break out, spread out, and parats YHWH perets, the LORD broke out a breach: the same root, parats, for David's plan and for the LORD's anger. The place is named Perez-uzza, the breach of Uzza.

  • v3 "we did not seek it in the days of Saul" — lo derashnuhu, the verb of 10:14, where Saul did not inquire of the LORD.

  • v5 "from the Shihor of Egypt to Lebo-hamath" — the full length of the land Joshua was told remained to be taken, from the Shihor, which is east of Egypt (Joshua 13:3, 5).

  • v6 "Baalah, that is, Kiriath-jearim" — the ark had stayed there since the Philistines sent it back, in the house of Abinadab on the hill (1 Samuel 7:1). Samuel calls the place Baale-judah (2 Samuel 6:2).

  • v7 "on a new cart" — the way the Philistines sent the ark home (1 Samuel 6:7). The law gave the sons of Kohath no carts, because theirs was the service of the holy things, which they carried on their shoulders (Numbers 7:9), and David's second attempt follows it (15:2, 15).

  • v9 "the threshing floor of Chidon" — Samuel has Nacon (2 Samuel 6:6).

  • v10 "because he put out his hand to the ark" — Samuel's for his error, al ha-shal, is a word found only there (2 Samuel 6:7); Chronicles names the act.

  • v14 "the LORD blessed the household of Obed-edom" — Obed-edom is the Gittite, a man of Gath, and his house is blessed while the ark is in it. In 15:18 and 16:5 an Obed-edom is among the Levite gatekeepers and musicians.
